chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from Al-Husayn ibn Khalid, from Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) used to say: 'The one who takes a ring whose stone is carnelian will not be impoverished, and judgment will not be passed for him except with that which is better.'

key_terms.لَمْ يُقْضَ لَهُ: Judgment is not passed for him

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and worldly benefits of wearing a carnelian ring according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Transmitted through the chain of Imam al-Rida (AS), this hadith from Al-Kafi underscores the enduring Sunnah of the Prophet and Imams in wearing carnelian rings, linking the physical act to divine blessings of sufficiency (ghina) and favorable judgment (hukm). In Shia tradition, the carnelian is not merely an ornament but a spiritual talisman that invites Allah's mercy, ensuring that one's affairs are resolved with 'that which is best' (allati hiya ahsan), a phrase echoing the Quranic ideal of ultimate success.
